description: f.lux on macOS via a use.computer remote sandbox. f.lux is a free menu-bar utility that adjusts the screen color temperature based on time of day to reduce eye strain. install_flux.sh downloads the official ~2 MB Flux.zip from justgetflux.com, extracts it to /Applications/, and strips quarantine; the binary is a universal (x86_64 + arm64) bundle so no Rosetta is required. setup_flux.sh writes baseline preferences via `defaults` (suppress Sparkle update prompts, seed a default location) and flushes cfprefsd. State lives in the per-user plist at ~/Library/Preferences/org.herf.Flux.plist (binary plist; key `wakeTime` is minutes-from-midnight, `lat`/`lng`/`place` hold location, `SU*` keys belong to the Sparkle update framework). Tasks currently shipped: `launch_flux` (smoke — pre_task launches Flux and verifier confirms LaunchServices registration), `set_wake_time_to_6am` (real — agent changes `wakeTime` from 480/8:00 AM to 360/6:00 AM via GUI stepper, `defaults`, or PlistBuddy; verifier scored against the on-disk plist with a strict wrong-target gate on protected fields).
